newsitem.title: DUBAI: ADNOC and IOC agree crude, LPG, product sales.
newsitem.headline: ADNOC and IOC agree crude, LPG, product sales.

text.p: Indian Oil Corp (IOC) will lift three million tonnes of crude from Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) in 1997 with an option for a additional one million tonnes, India's ambassador to the United Arab Emirates said on Monday.
The extra one million tonnes is subject is final approval from the Indian government.
"It is 90 percent sure they (IOC) will get the additional one million tonnes," said Murlidhar Menon, India's ambassador in Abu Dhabi, capital of the UAE.
IOC will also start lifting between 9,000 tonnes and 13,000 tonnes a month of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) from the UAE under a one-year contract beginning in January.
This is the first term LPG contract between the parties.
Under a 12-month contract IOC will also lift 500,000 tonnes of diesel and 300,000 tonnes of kerosene, Menon said.
No pricing information was immediately available.
IOC earlier this month signed up crude and product supplies with Kuwait Petroleum Corp and is expected to begin talks with Bahrain's Banoco later this week.
